remove_small_objects: Checks source dtype before out copy
out[:] is filled before later errors; out dtype chooses bool labeling versus integer bincount
max_size==0 returns copied/supplied out before count/negative-label/connectivity validation
Public deprecated min_size is rewritten by decorator into max_size: actual public threshold is inclusive <=, contrary to inner unreachable exclusive branch
Integer labels are global IDs even if disconnected; bool images use connected components
Only-one-integer-label warning and negative-label ValueError are observable
remove_small_holes: Integer input emits UserWarning and returns boolean
Explicit out must be bool, checked after integer-input warning
Inverts into out before component count errors; partial mutation on error is observable
Deprecated area_threshold is rewritten to inclusive max_size by decorator
Inner min_size deprecation warning is suppressed; outer FutureWarning remains
clear_border: Initial buffer validation uses labels.shape even with supplied out
Supplied out is not initialized from labels; existing out pixels are relabeled and cleared
Default full connectivity in component relabeling; disconnected equal integer labels are cleared independently
mask overrides border construction; mask must be bool and match out.shape
Mismatched mask shape currently raises TypeError: exceptions must derive from BaseException, due upstream raise-tuple
Input/outer out dtype preserved; scalar bgval assignment uses runtime NumPy casting/errors
Buffer comparison still occurs before mask-is-None short circuit, so nonnumeric buffer can fail even with mask
relabel_sequential: offset<=0 validated before input minimum; empty minimum error before dtype guard
Input negative minimum rejected before integer dtype validation
offset=int(offset) occurs after initial positivity/minimum check; positive fractional .5 can truncate to0
Labels assigned by sorted unique old values, not component traversal; 0 remains0
Output integer dtype uses required smallest unsigned type at overflow boundary; strict < max test changes int8 to uint8 when largest new label equals127
Output is fresh C-order array; mapping vectors are shared crosswise by forward and inverse maps

ArrayMap.scope: Additional returned class and constructor interface; separate native implementation is required before relabel API completion
state_contract: Constructor holds exact supplied key/value arrays without copies
Unknown and negative lookup keys map to0; scalar results retain NumPy scalar dtype
Boolean indexing flattens via nonzero positions; slices create integer index vectors
__array__ always allocates a fresh dense owned array and does not populate cache, even copy=False
First __setitem__ materializes _array; indices use dense NumPy semantics; nonzero compaction replaces key/value vectors and breaks inverse aliases
Failed first out-of-bounds __setitem__ still leaves dense cache materialized but original vectors/aliases intact
Maps retain data after source image and relabeled image lifetime ends
repr/str and configurable line truncation are observable
NumPy>=2.5 map_array out_view.shape assignment emits DeprecationWarning on successful mapping; indexing/call warning parity is checked against pinned original
Direct __len__ returns a NumPy scalar whose promotion/dtype depends on NumPy runtime; builtin len still returns Python int

NumPy1 uint64 max+1 promotes to float64: direct __len__ returns float64 while builtin len and dense __array__ raise TypeError even for tiny safe labels; functional integer lookup still works. NumPy2 retains unsigned integer scalar and these size operations work.
ArrayMap.constructor_test_scope: Bounded integer keys and float32 mapped values plus returned integer maps; not exhaustive all constructor dtype combinations
